subject: Pen test findings — requested remediation artifacts and compensating controls
messages:
From: Carol Simmons <carol.simmons@bluecrest.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amal Patel <amal.patel@bluecrest.com>, security@bluecrest.com
Date: 2026-09-28T09:15:00-04:00
Subject: Request: pen test report + remediation artifacts for June engagement

Neha,

Thanks again — Bluecrest completed our review of the June penetration test you provided. We have a few open validation items before we can sign off on the control remediation for our audit trail:

- Full pen test report (if any redactions were applied, please note them).
- Evidence that the three high findings (identified as RW-HIGH-1/2/3 in the summary) were remediated or mitigated: screenshots of patched systems, nginx config excerpt where the header was removed, and the internal ticket links.
- For the host where you noted a vendor-limited patch cadence and a compensating control applied, we need the exact ACL/WAF rule and a screenshot showing it in place.

Can you provide these artifacts as a single packet (PDF/zip) or point us to a secure shared folder? Target deadline for our audit team is 2026-10-08.

Appreciate it — we are trying to close this before year-end.

—Carol Simmons
Sr. InfoSec Manager, Bluecrest Finance
carol.simmons@bluecrest.com

Attachments referenced in our notes: Bluecrest_Summary_2026-09.pdf

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Carol Simmons <carol.simmons@bluecrest.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-28T10:02:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Request: pen test report + remediation artifacts for June engagement

On 2026-09-28 09:15, Carol Simmons wrote:
> Neha,
>
> Thanks again — Bluecrest completed our review of the June penetration test you provided...

Carol — thanks for the clear list. We'll assemble a remediation packet and aim to deliver by EOD 2026-10-05 (so you have a couple of days before your 10/8 internal review).

Quick confirmations so we send exactly what you need:
- You asked for the full PT report (any redactions ok) + artifacts for RW-HIGH-1/2/3 — correct?
- For the host with vendor-limited patching: is a screenshot of the IP allowlist + WAF rule plus a short note on why the patch couldn't be applied sufficient as compensating control evidence?

I've looped in Vivek (security lead) and Karthik (infra) to gather the tickets and screenshots. We'll summarize remediation steps and include links to the Jira entries and a downloadable zip.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Security Manager
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Carol Simmons <carol.simmons@bluecrest.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T14:30:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Request: pen test report + remediation artifacts for June engagement

Neha / Carol — quick status update from engineering/security: we have the remediation artifacts collected. Summary below and attachments will follow in a download link.

- PT report: RWX_PT_Report_2026-09-15.pdf (no redactions applied).
- RW-HIGH-1 (Open port misconfiguration): closed; config excerpt (nginx and host firewall) attached as config-excerpt-nginx.conf.txt; corresponding Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RW-SEC-457.
- RW-HIGH-2 (outdated library in connector): upgraded and unit-smoke tested; build artifacts + ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RW-INFRA-612.
- RW-HIGH-3 (vendor-managed appliance with delayed patch window): patch not possible within vendor SLA; applied compensating controls: network-level IP allowlist and managed WAF rule (rule id RW-WAF-2026-09-21). See waf-rule-snapshot.png and remediation-screenshots.zip.

We will export the three Jira issues into jira-export-RW-SEC-457.json and place everything in a time-limited Drive folder.

Let us know if you prefer the artifacts inline in email or a single signed PDF packet.

—Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Carol Simmons <carol.simmons@bluecrest.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amal Patel <amal.patel@bluecrest.com>, security@bluecrest.com
Date: 2026-10-02T08:22:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Request: pen test report + remediation artifacts for June engagement

Thanks Vivek — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying items before we accept the compensating controls: 

1) For RW-HIGH-1 we need the exact nginx directive lines and a before/after screenshot of the listening ports (netstat or equivalent).
2) For RW-HIGH-3 (vendor appliance) please include the vendor acknowledgement (email or ticket) that the patch cannot be applied within their SLA window, plus the exact WAF rule logic (not just an image) and proof that the rule is active and covering the affected endpoints.

If you can provide the vendor note and the configuration snippets / netstat output by EOD Monday 2026-10-05 we'll mark these items as provisionally resolved pending Bluecrest audit sign-off.

—Carol

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Carol Simmons <carol.simmons@bluecrest.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:45:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Request: pen test report + remediation artifacts for June engagement

Carol — attaching the packet and links per your ask. I included a short executive summary at the top of the Drive folder so your audit team can find the key artifacts quickly. Items attached / linked: 

- RWX_PT_Report_2026-09-15.pdf (full pen test).
- remediation-screenshots.zip (contains netstat_before_after.png, ip-allowlist.png, waf-rule-active.png).
- config-excerpt-nginx.conf.txt (shows the removed header and listen directive change).
- jira-export-RW-SEC-457.json (Jira export for the high finding).
- vendor-email-patch-window.pdf (redacted vendor acknowledgement that patching the appliance falls on their cadence; we included vendor ticket ID VEND-9981).

Specific callouts:
- RW-HIGH-1: nginx excerpt (lines 12-27 in config-excerpt-nginx.conf.txt) shows removal of the vulnerable header and change to the server listen directive. netstat_before_after.png confirms port 8089 was closed and service moved behind a proxy. Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RW-SEC-457.
- RW-HIGH-2: connector library upgraded; build SHA and smoke test logs included in remediation-screenshots.zip and Jira https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RW-INFRA-612.
- RW-HIGH-3: vendor cannot patch before their next maintenance window (vendor ticket VEND-9981). Compensating controls applied: IP allowlist on the perimeter (screenshot ip-allowlist.png) and WAF rule RW-WAF-2026-09-21. waf-rule-active.png shows the rule engine reporting "active" and matched requests over the last 7 days. The WAF rule logic is included as text in waf-rule-logic.txt inside the zip.

Download: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4d5E6F-BluecrestEvidence (access: link with expiration 2026-10-20). If you prefer, we can also assemble a single signed PDF packet.

Please confirm receipt and whether this satisfies your open items. Happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through any of the artifacts.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Security Manager
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: RWX_PT_Report_2026-09-15.pdf; remediation-screenshots.zip; config-excerpt-nginx.conf.txt; jira-export-RW-SEC-457.json; vendor-email-patch-window.pdf
